closing.note: Found it? Mark it on the map.

intro.text: László and Ilona opened Anton in February 2020 and got famous for their baking before they even had a Facebook page.

lines.text: Additive-free sourdough, laminated pastries and sweet and savoury buns.
Most cakes are made without sugar, except where the recipe can't do without.
Try the kanelbullar, the Swedish cinnamon buns.
Same owner as the Bageri micro-bakery near Parliament.

closing.note: Found it? Mark it on the map.

intro.text: A small specialty café in the Palace Quarter with its own Apricot Blend of Guatemalan, Colombian and Ethiopian beans.

lines.text: Getting the blend right took almost half a year and 40 kg of coffee.
Espresso drinks, plus V60, Aeropress and cold brew.
Open Mon–Fri 7–17, Sat 8–16, closed Sunday.

apricot.sources: We Love Budapest, Offbeat Budapest, Go Specialty Coffee
apricot.subtitle: Specialty coffee, house blend
apricot.title: Apricot Coffee

closing.note: Józsefváros lore, from the sources below.

intro.text: A self-governing community house, gig room and pub that gave a home to dozens of civil groups. It closed on 29 March 2026, when the owner didn't renew the lease.

lines.text: Opened in 2014 by the Marom Club Association, as a revival of the Sirály community space.
Housed groups such as the Roma Press Centre, Budapest Pride and the School of Public Life.
In 2017 the district withdrew its licence. The government office overturned that decision and Auróra reopened.
Its community built the Auróra Climate Garden on an old gravel car park, using only the city's green waste.
It said goodbye with a week-long farewell called Zárva Fesztivál, the Closed Festival, from 23 to 29 March 2026.

aurora.sources: We Love Budapest, HVG, XpatLoop, Front Line Defenders
aurora.title: R.I.P. Auróra

closing.note: Józsefváros lore, from the sources below.

intro.text: Rebuilding the square took 505 days and 3.68 billion forints.

lines.text: It added 80 trees to the ten already there.
On opening day people took the square back with tea and frantic dancing.

closing.note: Found it? Mark it on the map.

intro.text: Several taps and a terrace at the very start of Bródy Sándor utca, with the National Museum across the road.

lines.text: The street started out as gardens outside the old city walls and was once called Brick Street.
It has carried writer Sándor Bródy's name since 1949.
Full of students doing important research into the taps.

brody.subtitle: A beer institute by the Museum Garden
brody.title: Bródy Italintézet

closing.note: Józsefváros lore, from the sources below.

intro.text: A rooftop terrace on the fifth floor of the old Corvin department store, open from May 2007.

lines.text: The district closed it in 2018.
Game over, no continues.

corvinrip.place: BLAHA LUJZA TÉR · DEPARTMENT STORE ROOF
corvinrip.title: R.I.P. Corvin Club

closing.english: Vas utca · next to Bihary Watches
closing.note: Found it? Mark it on the map.

intro.text: Three old friends opened this café-meets-pottery studio in March 2025. Drink your coffee, then come back to make the cup.

lines.text: Coffee from early morning until 2pm. Workshops take over after that.
Fresh mugs and bowls dry at the back before going into the in-house kiln.
A minute from Blaha Lujza tér.

cozy.place: VAS UTCA · NEXT TO BIHARY WATCHES
cozy.subtitle: Ceramics workshop and specialty café
cozy.title: Cozy Studio & Café

closing.note: Found it? Mark it on the map.

intro.text: One of five market halls opened together in 1897, the year the city shut its street markets and moved the traders indoors.

lines.text: It's the everyday local market, not a show for tourists.
In 2012 the district named a whole new quarter after it: Csarnoknegyed.
Open Mon 6–16, Tue–Fri 6–18, Sat 6–13. Closed Sunday.

closing.note: Fecske: swallow, the bird.

intro.text: A cheap, laid-back presszó with a retro look and a terrace, a stone's throw from the Szabó Ervin Library.

lines.text: Weekday lunch menu at student prices.
Főfoto, the analogue photo café, lives upstairs.

fecske.subtitle: Student HQ with a lunch menu
fecske.title: Fecske

closing.note: Found it? Mark it on the map.

intro.text: A former private flat behind Kálvin tér, turned into a refuge for analogue photography. Ring the bell like you're visiting a friend.

lines.text: Opened in 2020 by János Krasznai and Gábor Zsigmond.
Sells film, slide projectors, photo books and cameras, and develops your rolls.
Shows Hungarian contemporary and classic photography.
The café side does sandwiches, pastries, coffee, beer and wine.

fofoto.subtitle: Café, gallery, lab and photo shop
fofoto.title: Főfoto

closing.note: Found it? Mark it on the map.

intro.text: Founded in 1771 and on this spot since 1847: 3.5 hectares of garden and 2,000 m² of greenhouses hidden behind the blocks.

lines.text: More than 8,000 plant species.
It's the garden from The Paul Street Boys. The novel is why the old name Füvészkert stuck.
Ticketed. Roughly 9–17 in summer and 9–16 in winter.
Look out for the spring sakura festival and the rare Victoria water-lily night openings.

closing.note: Found it? Mark it on the map.

intro.text: A small shop with a big rack of women's clothing.

lines.text: We couldn't confirm recent opening hours, so check it's open before you make the trip.
Do not feed after midnight.

closing.english: Gólya belongs to everyone. It's a cooperative.
closing.note: Szövetkezet: cooperative.

intro.text: Budapest's cooperative presszó: the people pouring your beer own the place. Bar, concert hall, rooftop and community house in one old industrial building.

lines.text: It started in 2013 on Bókay János utca and moved here in 2019, after the old landlord sold up.
The new home is about 1,200 m², renovated DIY style by a crowd of volunteers.
The programme runs from gigs and drag shows to board-game nights and conferences.
It shares the building with its sibling, Kazán Community House.

golya.sources: We Love Budapest, Spotted by Locals, Cooperative City
golya.subtitle: Cooperative pub, gig venue, community house
golya.title: Gólya

closing.english: The grund is ours! The rallying cry of The Paul Street Boys, the 1906 novel the pub is named after.
closing.note: Grund: an empty lot, the boys' playground.

intro.text: A sprawling, many-roomed pub around a courtyard with a tree. It works for daytime family drinks as much as late nights.

lines.text: Kid-friendly by day, with a playground in the courtyard.
The building turned 150 in 2023, the same year as Budapest itself.
Hosts the Grund Piac producers' and craft market.

grund.sources: We Love Budapest, Budapest by Locals
grund.subtitle: A huge pub with a tree inside
grund.title: A Grund

closing.note: Józsefváros lore, from the sources below.

intro.text: The Grund Kert community garden was cleared to make way for new Corvin Sétány housing.

lines.text: HVG reported a huge hole where one of the district's most colourful corners had been.

closing.english: Luxury hovel: the bar's own motto.
closing.note: Putri: a shack, said fondly.

intro.text: Hintaló means rocking horse, and yes, there are rocking horses among the ruin-pub junk-shop decor. Five minutes from Blaha.

lines.text: Two floors, Czech beer on tap and DJs on some nights, Wednesdays especially (says Lonely Planet).
Bacsó Béla utca became a pedestrian street in 2022 and was fully renewed in 2024, so there's room outside.
A crowd of locals and expats in roughly equal measure.

hintalo.sources: We Love Budapest, Lonely Planet, jozsefvaros.hu
hintalo.subtitle: The rocking-horse bar
hintalo.title: Hintaló Iszoda

closing.note: Found it? Mark it on the map.

intro.text: Baross utca splits it into a church side and a school side. This is where Józsefváros does its seasonal celebrations.

lines.text: Advent means Térvarázs: weekend concerts and family programmes.
A free 300 m² ice rink usually runs for about two months over winter.
In spring there's a craft and plant market.
The southern side is being redesigned after a resident survey that closed in January 2026.

closing.note: Found it? Mark it on the map.

intro.text: One of the biggest vintage floors in the country. The entire stock is swapped every five weeks, with big sales before each change.

lines.text: Near the end of a cycle, pieces can drop to a few hundred forints.
There's a sister shop at Astoria, on Károly körút.
Open daily 11–20, Sundays from 12.

closing.note: Found it? Mark it on the map.

intro.text: The art bookshop that started on Víg utca outgrew its room after six and a half years, moved to Baross utca and gained a plus sign.

lines.text: Founded by Beáta Istvánkó, who began it as a one-woman company.
Stocks the art books, catalogues and zines ordinary bookshops never get.
Has a screening room dedicated only to video works.
In autumn 2026 it showed ten years of Budapest Zines' riso printing.

isbn.sources: Lampoon, YKRA, Exindex, We Love Budapest, Telekom Spots
isbn.subtitle: Art bookshop, gallery and video room
isbn.title: ISBN+

closing.note: Found it? Mark it on the map.

intro.text: Gólya's sibling next door, run by SZAKI, the Alliance for Community Property Development. Kazán means boiler house.

lines.text: The building is a formerly abandoned transport manufacturing site, renovated with volunteers.
Social and cultural organisations share the space, and the rent stays affordable thanks to community ownership.
Runs the Kazán Energy Community, a co-owned local energy project.

kazan.subtitle: Community house with its own power
kazan.title: Kazán Közösségi Ház

intro.text: No joke on this one.

lines.text: After days stranded outside a closed station, about a thousand people, most of them Syrian, set off from here on foot for Vienna.

closing.note: Found it? Mark it on the map.

intro.text: The Fiumei Road cemetery, once called Kerepesi, covers 56 hectares and is known for its plants and wildlife as much as its tombs.

lines.text: Run by the National Heritage Institute (NÖRI) since 2016. Burials still take place here.
QR codes on the major sculptures and the FiumeiGuide app tell you whose grave you're looking at.
Mausoleums can only be visited by appointment, with a guide.

kerepesi.sources: Nemzeti Örökség Intézete, VG, We Love Budapest
kerepesi.subtitle: National graveyard, 56 hectares
kerepesi.title: Fiumei úti sírkert

closing.english: Break a single line of this sacred decree and you'll be chased out.
closing.note: Kergettetve: chased off, the Kerge way.
closing.text: Mely esetben eme szent rendelet egyetlen eleme meg lenne szege, el leszel kergettetve!

intro.english: Goat master! Come on in and make yourself at home. This is no booze pasture: it's the Kerge Society's sanctuary.
intro.text: Mekkmester! Gyere beljebb, leld kedved eme helyen mely nem egy szeszlegelde, de Kerge Egylet kegyhelye.

lines.english: Plenty of organised nights and mornings to enjoy, but you need to be a registered member. Put your name down and walk right in.
lines.text: Rengeteg szervezett estben s reggelben lelheted kedved, de ehhez neked Kerge Egylet feljegyzett egyede kell lenned, nevedet jegyeztesd fel, s mehetsz befele.

lines.english: One floor above you, decent folk may be drifting off to sleep right now. Let's not get reported. No hooliganism, turn your music down, or wander a little further off if inside isn't your thing.
lines.text: Ne feledd, fejed felett egy emelettel rendes emberek eme percekben szenderedhetnek el. Nem kellene ezek feljelentsenek… Ne fenegyerekeskedj, zeneszerkezetedet tekerd lejjebb, de elmehetsz egy cseppet messzebre mely esetben neked bent nem tetszene.

lines.english: Rolled one up? Find the spot that's meant for it.
lines.text: Megtekergetett dekkel kezedben lelj egy helyet mely erre rendeltetett.

lines.english: Like the cute cabinets? The billowing curtains? Don't wreck them, love them. They matter. (No mindless goat arranged all this.)
lines.text: Tetszenek eme csecse szekreterek? Esetleg eme fellengetett leplek? Ne cseszd el ezeket, szeretgesd meg ezeket, mert ezek szerepe elengedhetetlen (nem egy eszetlen kecske rendezte ezt be).

lines.english: There'll be nice people inside, so don't be unpleasant either. No playing Batman. Blend in instead.
lines.text: Kedves emberek lesznek bent, neked sem kellene kellemetlenkedned. Ne Betmenkedj, elehelyett elegyedj el.

lines.english: Need a hand? Seek out a Kerge insider.
lines.text: Kellene neked esetleg segedelem? Keress keserveddel egy Kerge-bennfentest!

kerge.note: Written in eszperente, the Hungarian word game where every single vowel is an e.
kerge.subtitle: The Kerge Society's decree
kerge.title: Kerge Egylet Rendelete

closing.note: Found it? Mark it on the map.

intro.text: Before the Four Tigers market was cleared, traders had already started moving across the road into the old Ganz-MÁVAG factory halls. They're still there.

lines.text: A maze of shops in huge former heavy-industry halls.
Small kitchens hide between the shops. Ask the people who work there where to eat.
Tram 28 from Blaha Lujza tér runs along Kőbányai út.

closing.note: Found it? Mark it on the map.

intro.text: The original Lumen: a small café and photo gallery with one of the most fought-over terraces in the district.

lines.text: It began as a café-gallery promoting contemporary photography, with a new exhibition every month.
Students by day. On summer evenings the terrace is close to impossible to get a seat on.
The square is named after writer Kálmán Mikszáth, who lived here. His limestone statue went up in 1960.

closing.note: Found it? Mark it on the map.

intro.text: The cellar pub students just call KK, inside ELTE's humanities campus. You don't need a student card, just the stairs.

lines.text: Open to everyone, whether you study humanities, law or nothing at all.
Live music turns up regularly, alongside DJ nights.
In summer its little sibling, the TreffOrt Kert terrace, opens in the courtyard. Heavy rain sends everyone back down to the cellar.

kk.subtitle: University cellar pub, open to all
kk.title: Könyvtár Klub

closing.note: Found it? Mark it on the map.

intro.text: Art historian and curator Kata Oltai's shop behind the Rákóczi tér market: animal prints, statement pieces and gloriously aimless clothes.

lines.text: It started in 2016 in a 16 m² room on Víg utca.
Every piece is one of a kind, so the stock changes daily.
Open Wed–Fri 15–19 and Sat 14–17. Plan ahead.
They often sell straight from Instagram and Facebook messages.

closing.note: Found it? Mark it on the map.

intro.text: Step inside and it's the year 2316: a rebel saloon where the staff play characters and the beer list is Hungarian craft.

lines.text: Opened in autumn 2016 as the city's first steampunk pub.
Most of the interior was made by hand. Cogwheels over circuit boards.
The kitchen leans British Isles: black pudding, haggis and pâté.
Runs craft beer tastings with a live blues show.

kraken.sources: XpatLoop, Daily News Hungary, Budapest by Locals
kraken.subtitle: Budapest's first steampunk saloon
kraken.title: Krak'n Town

closing.note: Found it? Mark it on the map.

intro.text: Finnish entrepreneur Ari Kupsus opened this gallery in 2009: contemporary art hung among early 19th-century antiques.

lines.text: A new exhibition roughly every month.
Funds scholarships for Academy of Fine Arts students, and one each year gets a debut solo show.
Neighbours on the street include Ani Molnár Gallery and Doxa.

closing.note: Found it? Mark it on the map.

intro.text: Barbi and Marci opened it in autumn 2025 on a corner Barbi spotted in an ad. The name was decided long before the place was.

lines.text: Fresh sandwiches, cinnamon and cardamom buns, and pastries from Ide Süss.
Evenings bring longer hours, mood lighting, short drinks and wine.
A small terrace on the Kőfaragó utca side.

kv.subtitle: Coffee by day, bar by night
kv.title: kv the coffee shop

closing.english: Two squares, one Lumen: the big one here, the small one on Mikszáth tér.

intro.text: The big Lumen: coffee and breakfast by day, Hungarian craft beer and wine by night, and live music in the back room.

lines.text: The Lumen story started on Mikszáth tér. This bigger room opened in 2017, when the square got too small for its crowd.
Jazz is a regular guest: free-improvisation nights and Budapest Jazzfest gigs have both played here.
A full kitchen, so the plants aren't the only thing being fed.

lumen.sources: We Love Budapest, Offbeat Budapest, JazzNearYou
lumen.subtitle: Café, bar and a tiny gig room
lumen.title: Lumen

closing.note: Found it? Mark it on the map.

intro.text: Once home to Jewish craftsmen and Roma musician families, the square went from run-down to lively after a renewal.

lines.text: First marked on an 1830 map as Frühlingsfeld (Tavaszmező). It has been Mátyás tér since 1874.
In the 1838 flood it stood under as much as three metres of water.
Writer Iván Mándy loved it, and film crews still come to shoot.
Stage of the Night of Gypsy Musicians.

matyas.sources: We Love Budapest, Kristin Faurest: Ten Spaces, jozsefvaros.hu
matyas.subtitle: Heart of the Magdolna Quarter
matyas.title: Mátyás tér

closing.note: Found it? Mark it on the map.

intro.text: Józsefváros never had a local history collection of its own until this museum opened in 2024, in the old Józsefvárosi Galéria rooms.

lines.text: The permanent show tells the district through objects and personal stories, not a timeline.
Its 38 topics were built from items and memories donated by residents.
Now and then it turns back into the old Jókai Café for Gypsy Music Café evenings.
Open Tue–Wed and Sat 10–18, Thu–Fri 13–19. Check before you go.

museum.sources: We Love Budapest, Budapest Times, jozsefvaros.hu
museum.subtitle: The district finally has a museum
museum.title: Józsefvárosi Múzeum

closing.note: Józsefváros lore, from the sources below.

intro.text: Rising rents pushed Gólya out of its old pub on Bókay János utca.

lines.text: It crowdfunded a building of its own on Orczy út.
Volunteers did much of the renovation.
Gentrification: 1. Storks: still flying.

oldgolya.sources: HVG, Index, Wikipedia HU, We Love Budapest
oldgolya.title: The Great Stork Migration

closing.note: Found it? Mark it on the map.

intro.text: A jumble of decades: old theatre gowns hang next to belts and scarves, with a second room full of everyday dresses.

lines.text: The owner, Ibolya Blázsev, has dealt in unusual clothes for decades.
Film and costume people shop here.
Good hunting ground for jewellery and 50s and 60s dresses.

prater.sources: XpatLoop, We Love Budapest, Lufthansa, Wanderlog
prater.subtitle: Two shops, one owner
prater.title: Vintage Shop Práter

closing.note: Józsefváros lore, from the sources below.

intro.text: Police searched Auróra for 14 hours and detained 15 people.

lines.text: They also seized industrial hemp grown for a sustainability programme.
A closure order followed in 2018. The place opened the next day anyway.
In 2019 the police turned up again, as surprise guests at a fundraiser.

closing.note: Józsefváros lore, from the sources below.

intro.text: A parked car dropped into a pit in the road about 2.5 m wide and 6–7 m long.

lines.text: The street had already been dug up again and again for utility works.
By 2016, residents described it as a street under siege.
Advice still stands: do not park on this tile.

sinkhole.subtitle: 18 NOV 2013
sinkhole.title: The Street That Ate A Car

closing.note: Found it? Mark it on the map.

intro.text: It looks puritan when it opens in the early afternoon. As the evening goes on, the sobriety wears off and the place fills up.

lines.text: A student favourite with reasonable prices.
Openly LGBTQ-friendly.
Deep in the Magdolna Quarter, a short walk from Teleki tér.

susuka.subtitle: The dorm club that forgot to close
susuka.title: Susuka

closing.note: Found it? Mark it on the map.

intro.text: The central branch of Budapest's biggest library network sits in the neo-baroque Wenckheim Palace, finished in 1889.

lines.text: The city bought the palace in 1927. After four years of conversion, the library opened here on 21 April 1931.
The reading rooms keep the palace's character, from a gold room to an old smoking room with a spiral staircase.
János Fadrusz's sculpted miners hold up the entrance.

closing.note: Found it? Mark it on the map.

intro.text: Teleki tér held the city's official junk market from 1897 to 1950. Today a renewed market hall runs the Teleki Zsibi community flea market.

lines.text: Zsibi days bring clothes, homeware, electronics, books and records, with music and food stalls.
2026 editions so far: 16 May and 4 July.
Market hall open Mon 7–16, Tue–Fri 7–17, Sat 6–14.
The park on the square was renovated together with residents, who formed an association to look after it.

teleki.subtitle: Market hall and community flea market
teleki.title: Teleki téri piac + Zsibi

closing.note: Józsefváros lore, from the sources below.

intro.text: A 39,000 m² container market, running since 1993, with more than 2,000 stall tenants at its peak.

lines.text: Bailiffs and police cleared it.
Traders crossed the road into the old Ganz-MÁVAG halls, and the game carried on. See Kiskína.

closing.note: Found it? Mark it on the map.

intro.text: Typo began on a gallery level under the old Corvin department store, sold from a warehouse for a while, then settled on Krúdy utca. Since winter 2025 it's called Momoko Vintage.

lines.text: Curated second hand with structure, for people who find chaotic thrift shops overwhelming.
Men's and women's collections with good labels.
Seasonal sales are worth watching for.

closing.note: Found it? Mark it on the map.

intro.text: A basement pub on the corner of Kiss József utca and Népszínház utca. Spot the big ZSÍR sign in the gloom, then go down.

lines.text: New owners opened it in 2022, in the space that used to be Hordo.
Cheap drinks, a properly mixed crowd and zero interest in pretending.
The heart of the Népszínház utca sidewalk festival, with bands playing right outside the door.
